name: Quebec City
tagline: The only walled city north of Mexico in North America, a French colonial capital crowned by a castle-hotel that looks lifted from a fairy tale.
highlight: Watching the sun set from Dufferin Terrace, Château Frontenac glowing above the St Lawrence River exactly as it has for well over a century.
shortDescription: The only walled city north of Mexico in North America, home to Château Frontenac, Old Quebec's colonial streets and Montmorency Falls nearby.
metaDescription: A Quebec City travel guide: Château Frontenac, Old Quebec, Dufferin Terrace, Montmorency Falls, food and how to plan a visit to Canada's colonial capital.
nearestAirport: Québec City Jean Lesage International Airport (YQB)
knownFor: Château Frontenac, Old Quebec's walls, Montmorency Falls

intro: Quebec City is genuinely the only walled city north of Mexico anywhere in North America, its Old Town a UNESCO World Heritage Site of French colonial architecture.
Towering above it all is genuinely Château Frontenac, a fairy-tale railway hotel so distinctive it's said to be the most photographed hotel on Earth.
Beyond the walls, genuinely dramatic Montmorency Falls sits just outside the city, taller than Niagara Falls even if considerably less powerful.

whyVisit.intro: Quebec City's case rests genuinely on being North America's most complete French colonial capital.

points.title: It's genuinely the only walled city north of Mexico
points.text: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with fortifications still fully intact.

points.title: Château Frontenac is genuinely one of the world's most photographed hotels
points.text: A fairy-tale silhouette that defines the entire city's skyline.

points.title: The Old Town is genuinely astonishingly well preserved
points.text: Cobblestone streets and stone buildings dating back centuries.

points.title: Montmorency Falls is genuinely a dramatic, easy add-on
points.text: Taller than Niagara Falls, and just outside the city.

points.title: It's genuinely even more French-feeling than Montreal
points.text: A smaller, more concentrated dose of Quebec's distinct culture and language.

attractionsIntro: Quebec City's essential sights are genuinely concentrated within and just outside its historic walled core.

attractions.name: Château Frontenac

image.file: File:Chateau Frontenac at dusk in Quebec City.jpg

attractions.text: Genuinely said to be the most photographed hotel in the world, a turreted 1893 railway hotel dominating the skyline.
attractions.tip: Genuinely worth a coffee inside even without staying — the lobby and terrace are open to visitors.

attractions.name: Dufferin Terrace

image.alt: Dufferin Terrace overlooking the St Lawrence River

attractions.text: Genuinely the city's grandest promenade, a boardwalk running along the clifftop beside Château Frontenac.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit at sunset for the best light over the St Lawrence River.

attractions.name: The Petit-Champlain quarter

image.alt: The Petit-Champlain quarter in Quebec City

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the oldest commercial streets in North America, steep and narrow, lined with boutiques and cafés.
attractions.tip: Genuinely take the funicular down from Dufferin Terrace rather than the steep stairs alone.

attractions.name: Montmorency Falls
attractions.text: Genuinely taller than Niagara Falls, a dramatic 83-metre waterfall just outside the city.
attractions.tip: Genuinely cross the suspension bridge at the top for a view straight down the falls.

attractions.name: Old Quebec's colonial streets
attractions.text: Genuinely a near-complete French colonial townscape, stone buildings and cobblestones dating back to the 17th century.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit early morning before day-trippers from cruise ships and tour buses arrive.

attractions.name: Château Frontenac illuminated at night

image.file: File:Chateau Frontenac illuminated at night in Quebec City.jpg

attractions.text: Genuinely a striking sight after dark, the hotel's copper roofs and turrets lit up above the city.
attractions.tip: Genuinely walk down to the Lower Town for a view looking back up at the illuminated hotel.

attractions.name: The House of Chevalier

image.alt: The House of Chevalier in Old Quebec

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the Old Town's best-preserved merchant houses, a glimpse into 18th-century Quebec commerce.
attractions.tip: Genuinely just one of many historic facades worth pausing for throughout the Lower Town.

thingsToDoIntro: Quebec City genuinely rewards unhurried wandering, split between the clifftop Upper Town and the riverside Lower Town.

thingsToDo.title: Walk Dufferin Terrace at sunset

image.file: File:Victoria Kiosk at sunset on Dufferin Terrace 2.jpg
image.alt: Sunset on Dufferin Terrace in Quebec City

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential evening ritual, watching the light change over the St Lawrence River from the boardwalk.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a lovely spot to simply sit on a bench and take it all in.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Petit-Champlain's boutiques
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to spend a couple of hours, browsing shops in one of North America's oldest commercial streets.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check the funicular's operating hours if you'd rather not walk back up the hill.

thingsToDo.title: Day-trip to Montmorency Falls
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely worthwhile half-day trip, a dramatic waterfall taller than Niagara just outside the city.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely take the cable car up rather than the stairs if you'd like an easier visit.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Old Quebec's walled streets
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding way to spend an afternoon, tracing centuries of French colonial history through narrow lanes.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely walk a stretch of the city's fortified walls for a different perspective on the Old Town.

thingsToDo.title: Listen to a street pianist on Dufferin Terrace

image.alt: A street pianist performing on Dufferin Terrace

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely charming, low-key pleasure, live music often drifting along the terrace in warmer months.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a nice reason to linger longer than you'd planned.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the Plains of Abraham
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely significant historic site, the battlefield park where a pivotal 1759 battle shaped Canada's future.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a peaceful green space today, popular for picnics and jogging as much as history.

foodIntro: Quebec City's food genuinely reflects the province's distinct culinary identity, from tourtière to maple products.

foods.name: Poutine

image.alt: Poutine, Canada's fries, cheese curds and gravy dish

foods.text: Genuinely born in rural Quebec, and Quebec City is genuinely a fitting place to try it.
foods.whereToTry: Restaurants throughout Old Quebec and beyond.

foods.name: Tourtière (meat pie)

image.alt: Tourtière, a traditional Quebec meat pie

foods.text: Genuinely a traditional Quebec comfort food, a spiced meat pie especially popular around the winter holidays.

foods.name: Maple products

image.alt: Maple sap, the source of Quebec's maple syrup

foods.text: Genuinely a real point of pride, with Quebec producing most of the world's maple syrup.
foods.whereToTry: Markets and specialty shops throughout the city.

foods.name: Quebec cheese
foods.text: Genuinely an underrated part of the province's food scene, with a genuine artisanal cheese-making tradition.
foods.whereToTry: Specialty cheese shops throughout Old Quebec.

foods.name: Caribou (traditional winter drink)
foods.text: Genuinely a quirky Quebec tradition, a fortified wine and spirit blend traditionally drunk during winter carnival.
foods.whereToTry: Bars throughout Old Quebec, especially during the winter carnival season.

foods.name: Fresh game and river fish
foods.text: Genuinely a nod to the region's hunting and fishing traditions, found on menus throughout the city.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional Quebec restaurants throughout Old Quebec.

accommodation.intro: Quebec City genuinely offers everything from budget guesthouses to Château Frontenac itself, with Old Town lodging commanding a premium.

areas.name: Within the city walls (Old Quebec)
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely immersed in the historic atmosphere
areas.text: The most atmospheric, though also the priciest, part of the city to stay.

areas.name: Just outside the walls
areas.bestFor: A genuinely better-value stay a short walk from the Old Town
areas.text: Easy walking distance to the main sights, with more modern accommodation options.

gettingThere.intro: Quebec City is genuinely well connected by train and road from Montreal, with its own smaller international airport.

options.text: Genuinely a comfortable, frequent option, no car needed.
options.detail: Takes about three hours via Via Rail's Central Canada corridor.

options.text: Genuinely a budget-friendly alternative to the train.
options.detail: Similar journey time, with more frequent departures than rail.

options.text: Genuinely available from a handful of Canadian and US cities.
options.detail: Québec City Jean Lesage International Airport sits about 20 minutes from downtown.

gettingAround.intro: Quebec City's genuinely compact walled core is entirely walkable, with a funicular connecting its two levels.

options.text: Genuinely the only way to properly explore Old Quebec.
options.detail: The Upper and Lower Towns are both compact and best experienced walking.

options.text: Genuinely the easy way to connect the Upper and Lower Towns.
options.detail: A quick, fun alternative to the steep stairs between the two levels.

options.mode: Bus or car to Montmorency Falls
options.text: Genuinely necessary for reaching the falls outside the city.
options.detail: A local bus or short drive covers the distance easily.

bestTime.headline: June to September for warm weather, or January to February for the Winter Carnival
bestTime.summary: Quebec City is genuinely a striking destination in both summer and winter, each offering a very different character.

seasons.text: Genuinely warm and lively, with outdoor terraces and festivals filling the calendar.
Genuinely comfortable temperatures with excellent fall colour throughout the region.
Genuinely magical under snow, especially during the Quebec Winter Carnival, though genuinely cold.
Genuinely a quieter shoulder season, with unpredictable weather as snow melts.

bestTime.avoid: Genuinely nothing strongly, though winter demands serious cold-weather gear.

itinerary.title: Two days in Quebec City
itinerary.intro: Built around Château Frontenac, the Old Town's two levels, and a half-day trip to Montmorency Falls.

days.title: Old Quebec
days.afternoon: The funicular down to Petit-Champlain and the Lower Town.
days.evening: Dinner in the Lower Town, with the illuminated hotel above.

days.title: Montmorency Falls and the Plains of Abraham
days.evening: A final dinner in Old Quebec.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Quebec City visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Wear genuinely comfortable shoes — Old Quebec's streets are cobbled and often steep.
Use genuinely the funicular to save the climb between the Upper and Lower Towns.
Learn genuinely a few basic French phrases — French is even more dominant here than in Montreal.
Visit genuinely Old Quebec early morning to avoid cruise-ship and tour-bus crowds.
Pack genuinely serious cold-weather gear for a winter visit.
Book genuinely accommodation well ahead for the Quebec Winter Carnival in February.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Quebec City?
faq.a: Two to three days genuinely covers Old Quebec and a trip to Montmorency Falls comfortably.

faq.q: Is Quebec City worth visiting compared to Montreal?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it offers a smaller, more concentrated dose of French colonial atmosphere, with Château Frontenac unlike anything in Montreal.

faq.q: Do you need to speak French in Quebec City?
faq.a: No, genuinely not, though French is even more dominant here than in Montreal, and a few basic phrases are genuinely appreciated.

faq.q: How do you get from Montreal to Quebec City?
faq.a: Genuinely easiest by train, taking about three hours via Via Rail's Central Canada corridor.
Yes, genuinely — at 83 metres, it's taller than Niagara Falls, and sits just outside the city.

faq.q: Is Quebec City good to visit in winter?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — the Winter Carnival in February is one of the city's real highlights, though it does require serious cold-weather gear.
